senses.gloss:
विट् विट् (also written बिट्; cf. rt. 1. विड्),
cl. 1. P. वेटति, वेटितुम्, to sound; to
curse, swear at, revile.

विट, अस्, m. a voluptuary; a paramour; (in the
drama) the companion of a prince or dissolute young
man or sometimes of a courtezan, (he resembles in
some respects the Vidūṣaka, being generally repre-
sented as a parasite on familiar terms with his asso-
ciate, but at the same time accomplished in the arts
of poetry, music, and singing); a catamite; a rogue,
cheat; N. of a mountain; the Khayar tree, Mimosa
Catechu; a medicinal salt (= विड्-लवण); a rat;
the orange tree; a branch and its shoot.
—१. विट-
प, अस्, m. a keeper of catamites.
—विट-प्रिय, अस्,
m. a kind of tree (= मुद्गर).
—विट-माक्षिक,
अस्, m. a sort of mineral (= ताप्य).
—विट-लवण,
अम्, n. a medicinal salt (= विड्-लवण, q. v.).

वीटा वीटा, f. a small piece of wood shaped
like a barley-corn and about a span long, (it was
struck with a stick or bat in a kind of game, like
hockey, played by boys; according to others the वीटा
was a metal ball of some kind; see Mahā-bh. Ādi-p.
5050, Schol.)

2. विटप, अस्, अम्, m. n. (according to Uṇādi-s.
III. 145. fr. rt. विट् in the sense ‘to sound’), the
young branch of a tree or creeper; a new shoot or
sprout, branch (in general); a bush; a clump, cluster,
thicket, tuft; spreading, expansion; the septum of the
scrotum.
—विटप-शस्, ind. in branches, in shoots.

विटपिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having branches; (ई), m. a tree
(in general); the large Indian fig-tree, Ficus Indica.
—विटपि-मृग, अस्, m. ‘tree-animal,’ a monkey,
ape; [cf. तरु-मृग.]

विटङ्क वि-टङ्क or वि-टङ्कक, अस्, अम्, m.
n. (see rt. टङ्क्), a dove-cot, an aviary (perhaps in
this sense fr. 2. वि, a bird, + टङ्क); the loftiest
point.

वि-टङ्कित, अस्, आ, अम्, marked, stamped, laden
with.

विटि विटि, इस्, f. yellow sanders.
—विटि-कण्-
ठी-रव, अस्, m., N. of the grammarian Varada-rāja.

वीटि वीटि, इस्, or वीटिका or वीटी, f. (said to
be fr. rt. इट् with वि), the betel plant, Piper Betel (=
ताम्बूल-वल्लिका); a preparation of the Areca nut
with spices and chunam enveloped in a leaf of the
betel plant, betel, Pān; a tie, fastening; [cf. वेत्र,
वेतस; cf. also Gr. ἴ-τυ-ς, ἰ-τέα; Lat. vi-tex, vitta,
vi-men, vi-ti-s; Old Germ. wi-d, wi-da; Angl.
Sax. widde.]

विट्कारिका विट्-कारिका, विट्-चर, &c. See
under 3. विष्.

विट्ठल विट्ठल, अस्, m. (or commonly विठ्-
ठल), N. of a god worshipped at Pandhar-pur or
Punderpoor in the Bombay presidency, (he is stated
to be an incarnation of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa himself,
who is believed to have visited this city); N. of the
author of the Prasāda commentary and of the Vaiṣ-
ṇava-siddhānta-dīpikā.
—विट्ठल-दीक्षित, अस्, m.,
N. of the author of the Kuṇḍa-maṇḍapa-siddhi.

विट्पण्य विट्-पण्य, विट्-पति, &c. See
under 2. विश्.
